# dutype

> Parallel disk usage analyzer that breaks a directory down by kind: file types (video, PDF, archives, ML models, data, code, ...) and special directories (node_modules, Python envs, .git, build output, package caches, ML caches). Interactive TUI for humans; JSON output and an MCP server for scripts and LLM agents. Written in Rust.

Agent usage: always pass `--json` or `--report`; plain `dutype PATH` opens an interactive TUI. Without an install, prefix commands with `npx -y` (e.g. `npx -y dutype --json PATH`).

- `dutype --json PATH`: totals, per-category shares, biggest children, biggest special dirs (cleanup candidates), biggest files. Paths are absolute, sizes are bytes allocated on disk (`size_bytes`, like `du`) plus a human string (`size`).
- Shared blocks (APFS clones on macOS, hard links): `freeable_min_bytes` is a lower bound of what deleting an item frees (not additive; quote it for cleanups), `dedup_bytes` counts each clone family once (additive), `clone_shared_bytes = size_bytes - dedup_bytes`, `accounting` says whether clones were detected and what is not considered (snapshots, partial clones). `--size-mode dedup` ranks lists by `dedup_bytes`.
- `dutype --json --category NAME PATH`: largest items of one category, e.g. `node_modules`, `Python env`, `Build output`, `Video`, `PDF`. Directory categories return directories, file categories return files.
- `dutype --top N`: list lengths (default 20). `--cross-fs`: descend into other mounts.
- `dutype --dump-config`: every category and its rules (TOML). Users extend them in `~/.config/dutype/config.toml`.
- `dutype --mcp`: MCP server on stdio with read-only tools `disk_usage` and `find_by_category` (arguments `path`, `top`, `cross_fs`, `refresh`, `size_mode`; same fields as `--json`).
